messages:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selection change we saw a spike in compaction time on paged-attn workloads during long-chat traces. Profiling attached below.

raj: saw the same in canary. p99 compaction_time went from ~12ms -> ~48ms for long sequences (>8k tokens).

sam: quick summary of what changed: runtime now prefers 'vectorized' kernel for mid-length sequences, falls back to 'compact-mode' for short sequences. The heuristic is slightly biasing toward vectorized for seq>2k.

jen: that heuristic seems to increase number of small-lived blocks and triggers more compaction cycles. Noticed higher kv-cache evictions as well.

maria: exact perf numbers from perf harness (reproduction run id: pr-2417):
```
baseline (old kernel heuristic): compactions=120, total_compaction_ms=1.4s, kv_evictions=8, p99_latency=78ms
after change: compactions=580, total_compaction_ms=8.9s, kv_evictions=46, p99_latency=112ms
OOMs observed: 0 -> 3 (during stress ramp)
```

kyle: interesting — compaction count x5. Any indication of block size churn?

sam: yes, allocator logs show many allocations around 48K-72K repeatedly. Blockmgr stats: avg_block_size dropped from 96KB -> 64KB and reuse_hit_rate fell from 0.72 -> 0.41.

raj: here's a minimal repro loop to run locally (uses perf harness):
```
./perf_harness --model paged-attn-test --seq 8192 --batch 3 --trace --duration 300
# collect blockmgr stats: curl localhost:9001/debug/blockmgr
```

jen: hypothesis: vectorized kernel path increases temporary per-request workspace fragmentation because it prefers many smaller temporary buffers. If block reuse heuristics are tuned for compact-mode, we get high churn.

maria: proposed quick experiments (low-risk):
- bump block size target from 64KB -> 128KB for paged-attn class
- increase reuse_window to keep blocks warm for 2x longer
- reduce eager_compact frequency (compaction cooldown backoff)
- add a corrective bias in kernel selector to prefer compact-mode when mem_frag_ratio > 0.25

sam: agree. Also try adjusting batching heuristics: limit batch multiplexing for seq>4k to reduce simultaneous ephemeral buffers. Could cut peak concurrent allocs.

kyle: small config diff I tried in a dev build (worked quick, not exhaustive):
```
--- a/runtime/blockmgr_config.h
+++ b/runtime/blockmgr_config.h
@@
- static constexpr size_t kDefaultBlockTarget = 65536; // 64KB
+ static constexpr size_t kDefaultBlockTarget = 131072; // 128KB
@@
- static constexpr uint32_t kReuseWindowMs = 500;
+ static constexpr uint32_t kReuseWindowMs = 1200; // keep blocks longer
@@
- static constexpr float kCompactionTrigger = 0.15f;
+ static constexpr float kCompactionTrigger = 0.28f; // be less aggressive
```

maria: thanks. That diff reduced compaction_count by ~2.3x in my quick run and lowered kv evictions by ~60%. p99 improved ~12ms. Still seeing 1 OOM during a 5m stress run though.

raj: can you paste the OOM trace?

maria: relevant snippet from device log:
```
[2026-02-12T15:02:11Z] alloc_request: 1.04GB
[2026-02-12T15:02:11Z] blockmgr: no free block large enough, attempting compaction
[2026-02-12T15:02:11Z] compaction: scanned 410 blocks, reclaimed 72KB
[2026-02-12T15:02:11Z] oom: gpu alloc failed at 1.04GB (cudaErrOutOfMemory)
```

jen: tiny reclaimed space despite scanning lots — indicates fragmentation. If compaction only reclaims small portions because hot blocks are pinned (KV cache), compaction cost is high and benefit low. Need smarter not just larger blocks.

sam: idea: preferentially avoid compacting blocks that are backing KV cache entries. Instead attempt lightweight defragmentation for ephemeral workspace buffers (sweep-only) and escalate to heavy compaction less frequently.

kyle: we can track block hotness via last_access_ts and a hot/cold watermark. Cold blocks are good candidates for eviction/merge. Hot ones should be kept for reuse.

maria: we should also consider reserving a small workspace buffer per-stream (on-demand) to satisfy transient spikes. Reserve size ~64MB total across device for paged-attn. If worst-case allocation hits reserved chunk, fall back to compact-mode kernel path to avoid OOM.

raj: put another way: add a soft-reserve quota for ephemeral allocations and a kernel fallback when reserve would be consumed. That buys graceful degradation.

jen: any measurable impact on latency from reserve+fallback?

maria: preliminary numbers: reserve enabled + fallback: p99 +6ms but OOMs zero during 10m stress. Without reserve p99 lower but OOMs observed. Tradeoff seems acceptable.

sam: we should add a metric: compaction_efficiency = bytes_reclaimed / compaction_time_ms. Use it to tune compaction_trigger adaptive threshold. If efficiency < threshold, back off for N seconds.

kyle: good idea. Also add a KV-safe compaction path: skip blocks with kv_pin_count>0 and attempt to merge adjacent cold blocks first.

maria: next steps:
- raj: wire kernel selector to check mem_frag_ratio and soft-reserve before picking vectorized kernels for long sequences (raj?)
- sam: implement compaction_efficiency metric and dynamic cooldown
- kyle: add hot/cold watermark and cold-first compaction policy
- jen: run 3 stress variants (baseline, blocksize128+reuse, blocksize128+reserve+dynamic_cd) and collect stats (compactions, reclaimed_bytes, kv_evictions, p99, OOMs)

raj: I'll take the kernel selector patch. Expect PR by EOD.

perfbot: scheduled perf run: pr-2417-variant-b at 2026-02-13T02:00:00Z (3 runs). Results will be posted here.

maria: thanks everyone. If you run local repro, drop raw blockmgr stats here. Even single-run logs help.

sam: dropping one more log excerpt from a failing run showing reuse misses: 
```
blockmgr.stats { total_blocks: 432, free_blocks: 62, avg_block_size: 65536, reuse_hits: 178, reuse_misses: 254 }
block_lifetime_hist:  <1ms: 34%  1-100ms: 40%  >100ms: 26%
```

jen: that lifetime hist suggests many very short-lived blocks — tuning reuse_window is low-hanging fruit.

maria: noted. I'll coordinate the PRs and merge order to make sure kernel selector and config changes land together. We'll reconvene after perfbot posts runs. :thumbsup:
